request.spec:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Retiring a person now works, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`. Something outside this app is using port 3000, so I ran it as `PORT=3417 bin/e2e`.

**Stored data and server**
- A new migration, `V16__person_retired.sql`, adds a nullable `retired_from` date to each person. A person with a date set counts as retired straight away, even if the date is after the sheet's today.
- A new `POST /api/people/retire` endpoint sets that date, using the sheet's today when none is given. It writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=… by=… name=… from=…` to the audit file.
- A claim dated after the person's retirement date is refused with an error (422), whether it is being added or edited. Claims dated on or before it are allowed. Quick-add goes through the same check, so a quick-add for a retired person is refused once the sheet's today is past their date.
- Retired people's claims still count in every total.
- The person data sent to the screen now includes retired yes/no and retired-from. Quick-add now sends the same person data instead of keeping its own copy.

**Screen**
- There is a "Show retired" checkbox (`show-retired`). It is off when the screen opens, and loading a sheet doesn't change it.
- Retired people have no row unless the checkbox is on.
- Each row shows `person-retired` (yes/no) and `person-retired-from`, plus a retire date field and a Retire button (`person-retire-date`, `person-retire`). A refused retire shows `person-error`.
- A claim refused for its date shows its own message in `claim-form-error`.

**Choices the request didn't cover**
- Retiring someone who is already retired is allowed and replaces their date.
- Retiring doesn't write a ROLLUP or TOTALS line to the audit file, because the totals don't change. The tests expect exactly this.

The test helpers also mention unretire and bulk retire, but this request doesn't ask for them, so I didn't build them.
